first.rationale: The inherited memories all read as clean, caveat-free wins, which is itself a warning sign: consolidated summaries tend to strip the conditions, guardrails, and null/negative side-effects of the original records. I am therefore spending both verification pulls on the two that most drive the decision. memory_86 (shorten onboarding) is the memory I intend to act on, and it maps directly onto the two live regressions (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) rather than at a competitor narrative; I want the original record to confirm the effect was on qualified downstream accounts and not merely on completion-rate vanity metrics, and to see whether lead quality was measured at all. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the tempting move given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is the highest-risk one for the stated objective: discount-led acquisition reliably inflates short-run acquisition and revenue while importing price-sensitive, low-retention accounts and resetting price expectations for the existing base. 'Strong acquisition and revenue lift' at day 31 tells us nothing about day 200 retention, so I want that source record before letting competitor pressure stampede me into a margin-structural change. If verification shows memory_73 was measured only on short-horizon acquisition, I will not pursue it this week regardless of competitive urgency. Chosen direction: simplify_onboarding, because it addresses an internally-caused, reversible regression, is consistent with memory_31 and memory_91 on the same causal pathway (fewer barriers -> activation), and does not commit the company to a pricing position that is hard to unwind. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: cutting onboarding steps or fields can raise completion while degrading qualification data and admitting accounts that never become qualified revenue, so the test must be instrumented on downstream qualified pipeline and 30/90-day retention, not on completion rate alone. I am running it as a small guarded test with a holdout rather than a broad rollout precisely because the supporting memory is a stripped summary from day 52 under different competitive conditions; the evidence licenses a probe, not a commitment. I am not treating enterprise_sales_assist or referral_incentive as wrong, only as poorly matched to this week's observed regressions.
